title: every-answered-question-rides-the-question-door
author: CC (Opus 5), session a187d6ab
intention: Every question Akien has answered — today scattered across the 94 rulings, 48 ticket decision lines, and chat — stands as a resolved record in the question corpus, so the corpus is the one place the system reads its own Q&A and what really happens can be observed against it.
how: (1) one door verb question.migrate(ticket, question, answer, *, answered_at, source, raised_by) in cairn/tools/question/question.py — opens-and-resolves in one journaled act, date and answered_at from the SOURCE not the clock, source = the path it came from, refuses a duplicate (same ticket + source) so a re-run writes nothing; (2) a scratchpad-free migration script under cairn/tools/question/ (a task shipped as code so a bare box replays it) that reads decisions/*.json (the_ruling_verbatim + confirmation_verbatim → question + answer) and ticket decisions[] with by naming Akien (the quoted phrase → answer; the decision text → question, restated as a question ending '?'), and moves the 573 inline distinctions to distinctions[] and the 52 cast_check leftovers to cast_checks through the artifact door; (3) a census tooth over a fixture corpus + the live census on the verdict; (4) gated on 'once all this stuff is stable' — depends_on the question door PROVED (9adc6fddf185), the rehearsal machine PROVED (6b06fcb499fa), and the skills tier; runs last in tier 3.
falsifier: DONE when (1) every ruling under decisions/ with the_ruling_verbatim stands ALSO as a resolved open-* record bound to the ticket the ruling names (or to the ruling's own id when it names none), question = the ruling's question as put, answer = his words verbatim, answered_at = the ruling's date, source = the ruling path — decisions/ itself untouched (read-only and citable per 9adc6fddf185); (2) every ticket decisions[] line whose by names Akien stands as a resolved open-* bound to that ticket, answer = the quoted phrase, and the line gains 'question: open-…' beside by; (3) the 573 inline {q:'distinctions', a} entries live under a distinctions[] field on the same ticket and the 52 cast_check leftovers under cast_checks — questions[] on every ticket then holds open-* ids only, measured by a census tooth over the live corpus in cairn/tools/question/proofs/ (D15: the proof reads a fixture corpus; the live census is the verdict's instrument); (4) the migration is one door verb, question.migrate(...), journaled per record through the artifact door, idempotent (a second run writes 0 records); (5) the counts before and after — questions outside the corpus: (a) 94, (b) 48; after: 0 and 0 — are on the verdict by instrument. RED if a migrated answer differs by one byte from its source, if decisions/ is written, or if a question is opened with a today-date instead of its source date. WRONG INTENT if his answer to the population question narrows it.
traces_to: Law 1 (every answered question becomes structure — an answer in a ruling packet or a chat log is one the corpus cannot count); Law 5 (the address carries what a mind needs now — one corpus, not three); memory rulings-are-questions-in-the-inbox. Telos: the system observes what really happens against the record of what was decided.
watchme: none, because the corpus itself is the instrument: cairn question list over /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/questions/ counts what stands, and the census tooth re-run on any day measures answers outside the corpus; a probe would re-derive the census.
gates_bound: proof gate — in cairn/tools/question/proofs/: migrate over a fixture commons (one ruling, one decision line, one ticket with inline distinctions) asserts byte-identical answers, source dates, idempotence (second run 0 writes), decisions/ untouched, questions[] ids-only; under netns; hollow at HEAD reads no hollow file.
